\section[o ordenado]{o ordenado — the salary, the wages}

\label{lesson:PT-C362-ordenado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for efficient, then the Portuguese for the productivity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o ordenado}
\textbf{o ordenado} — \textquotedblleft{}the salary, the wages\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O ordenado chega no fim do mês.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The salary arrives at the end of the month.}
\end{quote}

In Portugal \emph{o ordenado} and \emph{o salário} are both common.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ordenado} is the participle of \emph{ordenar} \textquotedblleft{}to order, to arrange\textquotedblright{} used as a noun, through Old Portuguese \emph{ordenado} (EtymDB); \emph{ordenar} is inherited from Latin \emph{ōrdināre} \textquotedblleft{}to set in order\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{ōrdō} \textquotedblleft{}order\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o ordenado}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o ordenado}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o ordenado}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for efficient, then the Portuguese for the productivity, then say \emph{o ordenado} again

\section[o subsídio]{o subsídio — the allowance, the benefit; the subsidy}

\label{lesson:PT-C362-subsidio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the productivity, then the Portuguese for the salary.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o subsídio}
\textbf{o subsídio} — \textquotedblleft{}the allowance, the benefit; the subsidy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O subsídio de férias ajuda a pagar a viagem.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The holiday allowance helps to pay for the trip.}
\end{quote}

In Portugal many workers get two extra months of pay a year: \emph{subsídio de férias} and \emph{subsídio de Natal}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{subsídio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{subsidium} \textquotedblleft{}troops in reserve, help\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{subsidere} \textquotedblleft{}to settle, to stay behind\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{sedēre} \textquotedblleft{}to sit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[negociar]{negociar — to negotiate}

\label{lesson:PT-C362-negociar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the salary, then the Portuguese for the allowance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: negociar}
\textbf{negociar} — \textquotedblleft{}to negotiate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O sindicato negociou um ordenado melhor.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The union negotiated a better salary.}
\end{quote}

Also to trade: \emph{negociar em vinho}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{negociar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{negōtiārī} \textquotedblleft{}to carry on business\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{negōtium} \textquotedblleft{}business\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{nec} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ōtium} \textquotedblleft{}leisure\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a reforma]{a reforma — the retirement, the pension; the reform}

\label{lesson:PT-C362-reforma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the allowance, then the Portuguese for to negotiate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a reforma}
\textbf{a reforma} — \textquotedblleft{}the retirement, the pension; the reform\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O meu avô está na reforma há dez anos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My grandfather has been retired for ten years.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese for retirement; in Brazil \emph{a aposentadoria}. Also a reform: \emph{a reforma da escola}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reforma} is built on \emph{reformar} \textquotedblleft{}to reshape\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{refōrmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to shape again, to transform\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), on \emph{fōrma} \textquotedblleft{}shape\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[reformado]{reformado — retired}

\label{lesson:PT-C362-reformado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to negotiate, then the Portuguese for the retirement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: reformado}
\textbf{reformado} — \textquotedblleft{}retired\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A minha mãe é reformada: era professora.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My mother is retired: she was a teacher.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese; in Brazil \emph{aposentado}. Also a noun: \emph{os reformados}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reformado} is the participle of \emph{reformar}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{refōrmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to shape again, to transform\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
